node.title: Re: Test post for <code> and <pre>
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
the generates a monospace text in the tiny font size.

You might want to enable the option "Large Code Font" in your [id://450961].

Generally, or tags should be used for all code, sample input, output, etc. They do not interpret any other tags or PerlMonks [...] links inside them, and they provide the [download] link. (Update: Note that tags are a special feature of PerlMonks and are not the HTML5 tags.)

 tags are just HTML formatting tags; they no not prevent the interpretation of other HTML tags or PM [...] links inside them, and AFAIK get no special processing from PM. The only advantage they have is that they support Unicode, while  tags unfortunately do not; but you still have to escape all the <>&[] characters inside 
 tags. (Combining  and 
 doesn't make sense.)
